idiom_name: class method composed of private method calls
implementation_notes: A class method whose body only calls other methods is the plain TypeScript realization; private is checked by the compiler and erased at runtime, while an ECMAScript #private method is enforced by the runtime and invisible to plain-JavaScript callers of the compiled output. Choose private for the familiar, subclass-friendly form and # when the boundary must survive outside TypeScript; module-scoped functions compose the same way when a step needs no instance state.
pitfalls: TypeScript private disappears at runtime: (checkout as any).reserveStock() still works, so the modifier documents intent rather than enforcing it.
#private steps are unreachable from subclasses; a step that must be overridable has to be protected, and mixing # and protected in one hierarchy is a common source of surprises.
Unannotated step signatures widen implicitly, so the coordinator's contract can drift from the steps' - annotate step parameters and return types.
